title: How Two Rows of Teeth Become One Zipper

lines.say: Two tapes. Hundreds of teeth. One slider.
The rows never line up. One is shifted by half a tooth.
The whole chain? Five millimetres wide. So how do they grab?
Every tooth has a bump on top... and a hollow underneath.
Push them straight together, and they jam.
Inside the slider: a Y-shaped channel.
It tilts each tooth just enough to clear the next.
Bump into hollow. Click. Over and over.
But here's the catch: no zipper is ever fully closed. The wedge has to stay between the last teeth.
Pull down, and that wedge pries them apart.
Lose one tooth, and the whole chain gives way.
The biggest maker builds over seven billion a year.
Glass bottle, or ballpoint pen? Comment below.
